title: Set up a weld radiograph: IQI wires across the weld, lead markers at both end ticks
instruction: This butt-welded plate is being set up for its radiographic test shot. The film goes under the plate, so the top of the plate is the side the shot is taken from. The painted stripe is the weld, and the two painted ticks across it mark the ends of the length this shot covers. Place the wire-type image quality indicator and the two lead location markers (0 and 1) where ASME Section V requires them for this shot, then let go of them.
context: Industrial radiographers set up every weld shot before the exposure. ASME Section V, Article 2 fixes where the reference objects go: the image quality indicator (IQI) on the source side of the part, and a wire-type IQI on the weld with the length of its wires perpendicular to the length of the weld (T-277.1); location markers on the part, not on the film holder, so their images show the coverage at each end of the area of interest, on the source side for flat parts (T-275, T-275.1(a)(1)). The wires' images prove the shot's sensitivity across the weld, and the markers tie the film to the weld so a defect can be found again; a film without a valid IQI or markers is rejected and the weld shot again. Here the wire IQI starts on the bench with its wires along the weld, so carrying it straight across lays it the wrong way, and the markers start beside the arms, away from the ticks.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Welded plate, fixed to the table: two grey steel plates butt-welded along y, 160 mm (x) by 200 mm (y) in all and 10 mm thick, spanning x 28.0 to 44.0 cm and y -10.0 to +10.0 cm. The weld runs along y across the plate's middle: a dark grey cap 14 mm wide (x 35.3 to 36.7 cm, centreline x 36.0 cm), ground flush with the plates' tops, over the plate's whole 200 mm. (2) Two shot-length ticks: yellow painted strips 24 mm (x) by 4 mm (y), 0.5 mm thick, on the plate's top across the weld (x 34.8 to 37.2 cm), their centre lines at y -8.0 and +8.0 cm: the ends of the 160 mm this shot covers. (3) Wire IQI, loose: a clear light-blue plastic holder 55 x 28 x 12 mm, 15 g, with six dark steel-grey wires sealed along its 55 mm length, shown as dark strips 50 mm long on its top face, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6, 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 mm wide at a 4 mm pitch (0.5 mm proud). It lies flat on the table in front of the plate, centred at x 23.0 cm, y 0, wires along y (parallel to the weld), wires up. (4) Two location markers, loose: grey plastic blocks 22 x 22 x 12 mm, 15 g each, each holding a lead figure shown as a white figure 0.5 mm thick on its top, '0' on one and '1' on the other, the top of each figure toward +x. Marker 0 lies flat on the table centred at x 24.0 cm, y -16.0 cm, marker 1 at x 24.0 cm, y +16.0 cm, both square to the table edges. The film is taken to be under the plate (not modelled); the plate's top face is the source side. Nothing else is on the table. Real wire IQIs and lead figures are thin; these are 12 mm blocks so a gripper can hold them.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the three parts' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a rule on a top photo). A part is released when each gripper's finger zone (a cylinder round the gripper's axis from the point between its pad tips 38 mm up, out to a pad's outer corner) stays 10 mm or more from it over the last 0.5 s, and settled when its centre moved under 2 mm in all and its heading under 1 degree in that 0.5 s; it counts when released and settled. Still for 1 s: settled in each of the last two 0.5 s windows and released throughout. A part lies on the plate when it is flat (within 5 degrees of level, either face up), its centre is over the plate and its lowest point is within 3 mm of the plate's top (not on the table, on another part or held up). The IQI is correct when it counts, lies on the plate, its wires are within 8 degrees of x (perpendicular to the weld), its centre is within 15 mm of the weld centreline (x 36.0 cm), so every wire crosses the whole weld, and every corner of its footprint is between the ticks' centre lines (|y| at most 8.0 cm). A tick has a correct marker when a marker counts, lies on the plate, and its centre is within 10 mm of that tick's centre line along the weld (y) and within 35 mm of the weld centreline (x): on or beside the weld. Either marker may be at either tick; two at one tick count once. Markers count only when the IQI is correct. First match wins: IQI correct, both ticks with a correct marker and all three parts still for 1 s: 1.0. IQI correct and at least one tick with a correct marker: 0.75. IQI correct, no correct marker: 0.5. IQI counted and lying on the plate but not correct (wires along the weld or more than 8 degrees off x, centre more than 15 mm off the weld centreline, footprint past a tick): 0.25. Otherwise 0: the IQI on the bench or the table beside the plate (the film side), on its side or an edge, on a marker, still held or moving. Examples: the IQI across the weld with a marker at each tick, 1.0; the same with one marker left on the bench or both at one tick, 0.75; both markers beside the IQI 45 mm from the ticks, 0.5; the IQI laid along the weld, with or without markers, 0.25; nothing moved, 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. No radiation, film or image is simulated; the weld is a flat dark strip flush with the plate, and the IQI and lead figures are 12 mm blocks with painted wires and figures rather than a thin wire pack and 2 mm lead characters, so the fingers can grip them. Their places are full size and as the code states. The grippers are read only to check that each part was let go.
reset_notes: Lay the wire IQI back flat on the table centred at x 23.0 cm, y 0, its wires along y (parallel to the weld) and up; marker 0 flat at x 24.0 cm, y -16.0 cm and marker 1 flat at x 24.0 cm, y +16.0 cm, square to the table edges, figures up with their tops toward +x. The plate, weld and ticks are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
